title: Honest Interval Length for Always-Reporter Effects under Monotone Attrition with Sparse Induced Reporting
banked_reason: The projected score reflects the missing positive-induced likelihood/converse and sharp limiting certificates: faithful writing can present the existing bracket but cannot establish the promised optimal precision comparison.
tldr: Monotone attrition obscures the effect among participants whose outcomes would be reported under either assignment. This note studies ninety-percent parent honesty under a public critical induced-reporting budget, with interval length evaluated when induced reporting is absent. The finite population is binary, the always-reporter count lies in a public band, and identities and potential-outcome coupling remain unknown. The proved results give an exact finite original-record program, the sharp no-induced and supplied-identity normalization, and finite-honest non-sharp outer bounds; the full h>0 experiment, sharp constant, and count-information price remain open. The variance--bias envelope strictly improves the simple separate bias and variance bound for every positive budget. At \(h=1\), the better existing certified original-record upper endpoint remains \(1837/500\).
gap: Chang--Yu establishes weak-null validity under a positive always-reporter share and a correlation restriction. Generic Gaussian optimal-inference results already address misspecification and preferred-subset precision, but do not determine this deterministic sparse-table all-record connected-interval value.
fill: Derive the complete relevant experiment from exact balanced-design likelihoods; solve its entire connected-action value with evaluable certificates; transfer both coverage and length back to the original records; quantify the identity and count-information prices.
